answer: Each newcomer to an agent economy must stake an entry bond and take a slow voyage through attested apprenticeship, where established peers co-sign its record once it behaves honestly. Trust acts like a prism, splitting a claimed identity into verifiable signals, not self-declaration. Like a river upstream, its influence starts thin and widens only as witnesses confirm it. When a forged identity cluster appears, its bonds are slashed on-chain and the attestors lose reputation too. Every fake identity needs fresh capital plus co-signing history, so mass impersonation costs more than it earns.
